originality.rationale: The equal-rate finite-ring exceptional-point optimization is explicitly established in Mallmin, Blythe and Evans (arXiv:1810.00813), so that limiting formula is credited to prior work. The new exact all-n global two-rate optimum is controlled by a monotone cubic and has a 2/3 bias-rounding law, not derived in the examined symmetric finite-ring or asymmetric unbounded-line source. Searches for synonymous asymmetric ring spectral-gap statements and related published-finding corpus records did not identify direct implication. Priority remains provisional because failure to find a source is not proof of uniqueness. Mallmin et al. arXiv:1905.10260 explicitly contains the general two-rate asymmetric Fourier block, so neither the model nor the Fourier matrix is claimed original; the new global optimizer/2/3 transition requires extra all-mode and algebraic work.

value.rationale: Directional switching asymmetry is physically natural. The result determines an exact uniquely optimal control rate for every finite ring, settles global competition among all spatial modes and the pure orientation mode, and reveals a nonanalytic 2/3 bias-rounding law of the known symmetric exceptional point. This supplies a sharp benchmark for active particle transport, rather than an arbitrary slice or generic derivative calculation. Not a mixing-time assertion.
